Digital twin demo

Source: vignettes/articles/twin-app.Rmd
twin-app.Rmd

This interactive demo builds a patient’s digital twin with simulateTrajectory(), as in Digital twins, and runs in the browser with no R needed. Pick a patient from the pbc3 data, or upload one patient’s follow-up visits as a CSV file. The interface is available in English and Chinese.

If the frame does not load, open the demo in a new tab. On the free hosting plan the app goes to sleep when nobody is using it, so the first visit can take up to a minute to start.

What the demo shows

The app fits the sub-models once, when it starts, on pbc3: a Cox model for death or transplantation (status3), a logistic model for which of the two occurred (status4), and linear mixed models for three biomarkers (log serum bilirubin, albumin and log prothrombin time). The twin is a set of futures drawn from the model, conditional on the patient’s measurements up to the year it is built at.

Replay the twin. Move the “Twin built at year” slider, or press its play button, and the twin is rebuilt from the measurements up to that year. The forecast biomarker is shown as a median and 90% band. The measurements the twin used are filled points, and the ones taken later are open points, so you can see how the forecast compares with what happened. Next to it are the forecast probabilities of death and of transplantation. For the example patients, the patient’s actual outcome is marked as well.

Ask the twin. A sample of the simulated futures is drawn as one line each, ending at its event. The twin then answers questions from all of its futures:

  • the probability of death, of transplantation, or of either, within a chosen number of years;
  • the probability that a biomarker goes above or below a threshold before any event, and the probability that the patient is event-free and past the threshold at a chosen time;
  • the median year of the event, and the probability of being event-free through the end of the forecast.

The twin is a statistical, predictive model of outcomes as observed in the data it was fit on, not a mechanistic or causal model of the disease.

Uploading a patient

The CSV needs one row per visit and the columns year, age, sex, serBilir, albumin and prothrombin, on the same scales as pbc3. The app has a template you can download. Visits after the year the twin is built at are not used by the twin, but are shown as open points.

Running the app locally

The app’s source is in the shiny/bjm-twin folder of the repository. To run it on your own computer, clone the repository and run:

install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib"))
shiny::runApp("shiny/bjm-twin")

The demo is for illustrating the method only. Its models are fit on the PBC data set and must not be used for clinical decisions.
